Just why is bitcoin so valuable?
It has widespread use, and the number of different safety features people have built into it make it actually useful as a medium for currency exchange.

So value is a function of supply and demand.

If something has any demand at all, and a limited supply it will have value.

/v/Bitcoin provably has limited supply, and it's not controlled by any single entity.

It was designed to act a lot like gold, to have a fixed amount of extractable value (analogous to the amount of gold in the ground) that is extracted at a fairly predictable rate and not centralized to any single location.

Now why does it have demand?

Well a lot of people want an alternative to the USD, gold is impractical to use for what people tend to use currency for these days; and bitcoin has the (dis?)advantage of being a purely digital thing, which makes it exceedingly easy to transact with online.

It's only difficult to use because of the restrictions put on money exchange by governments, which makes it hard to purchase or sell bitcoin, but once you have bitcoin everything is a lot more painless.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Network_effect are the main reason that bitcoin vastly out values other currencies, same reason social networks besides Facebook are hard to grow.

But /v/ethereum is showing that if you add additional features that people demand, you can start to carve out your own niche.

From a technical/security perspective it is also thought that the more people mining a crypto currency, the more secure it is, this kind of plays in with network effects, but when people are talking about how bitcoin is the worlds biggest supercomputer they are coming at it from this angle.
